source_text: Χρὴ δὲ εἰδέναι ὅτι οἱ μὲν πρότεροι τοῦ εὐαγγελικοῦ γενόμενοι φίλοι γράμματος, καὶ μὴ ἐπιστήσαντες ὅτι καὶ ταῦτα ἐν παραβολαῖς ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ πνεύματι εἴρηται, ἐξωμάλισαν ἀκολούθως τοῖς προτέροις δύο τὸν τρίτον· τῷ γὰρ σωματικῶς λελέχθαι τοὺς δύο ἕπεται καὶ τὸν τρίτον εἶναι σωματικόν. Οἱ δὲ δεύτεροι τῷ μὲν τρίτῳ ὑγιῶς ἐπιβεβλήκασι τὴν ἀπὸ λόγου ἐκτομὴν τοῦ παθητικοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς ψυχῆς νομίσαντες δηλοῦσθαι, οὐκέτι δὲ τεθεωρήκασιν ὅτι ἁρμόζον ἦν καὶ τὰς προτέρας δύο ἀλληγορικῶς ἐκλαμβάνειν. Εἰ δὲ ἐπὶ ἄλλοις τόποις λέγειν πάρεστι «Τὸ γράμμα ἀποκτείνει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζωοποιεῖ», τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ ἐνθάδε φατέον· ἡ τηρηθεῖσα περὶ τῶν δύο εὐνουχισμῶν γραμμὴ ἀπέκτεινε τοὺς τὸν τρίτον ὡσαύτως νοήσαντας. Εἰ δέ τις καὶ ἐφ’ ἑτέρων παραδειγμάτων βούλεται δεῖξαι τὴν Καινὴν Διαθήκην γράμμα ἀποκτεῖνον ἔχουσαν, ἀκουέτω πῶς ὁ Σωτὴρ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις φησίν· «Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων, μή τινος ὑστερήσατε;» εἶτα «νῦν ὁ ἔχων βαλλάντιον ἀράτω ὁμοίως καὶ πήραν, καὶ ὁ μὴ ἔχων πωλησάτω τὸ ἱμάτιον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀγορασάτω μάχαιραν.» Ὁ γὰρ μὴ νοήσας καὶ μάχαιραν φονικὴν ἀγοράσας ἀπολεῖται παρὰ τὴν βούλησιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ κακῶς τὸν λόγον ἐκλαβών. Δόξα Χριστῷ. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The letter kills: two readings of the three eunuchisms
orientation: Origen is concluding his discussion of the three kinds of eunuchs, distinguishing two groups of earlier interpreters and applying the principle that the letter kills but the Spirit gives life.
pass_a_gloss: But it is necessary to know that the first friends of the gospel letter, and not having noticed that Jesus spoke these things also in parables and they were said in spirit, leveled out the third in accordance with the first two; for from the two having been said bodily it follows that the third also is bodily. But the second group applied to the third soundly the cutting out of the passionate part from the soul by reason, thinking it to be indicated, but they no longer observed that it was fitting also to take the first two allegorically. But if on other passages it is possible to say 'The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life,' the same must be said also here; the kept line about the two eunuchisms killed those who understood the third in the same way. But if someone also wishes to show from other examples that the New Testament has a letter that kills, let him hear how the Savior says to the apostles: 'When I sent you without purse and bag and sandals, did you lack anything?' then 'now let the one who has a purse take it likewise also a bag, and let the one who does not have sell his cloak and buy a sword.' For the one who did not understand and bought a murderous sword will perish against the will of Jesus, having taken the word badly. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the genitive of relationship and the personification of the letter, matching Origen's contrast between letter and spirit.
The verb means to make level or smooth; it conveys the flattening of the third kind into the same bodily sense as the first two.

choices.term: ἡ τηρηθεῖσα περὶ τῶν δύο εὐνουχισμῶν γραμμή
choices.english: the kept line about the two eunuchisms
choices.why: γραμμή here is the literal line of interpretation; 'kept' preserves the perfect passive participle's force of holding fast to it.

choices.term: ἀπολεῖται παρὰ τὴν βούλησιν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ
choices.english: will perish against the will of Jesus
choices.why: παρὰ with accusative means against or contrary to; this preserves the sense that the literal sword-buyer perishes contrary to Jesus' intention.
rejected: will perish beyond the will of Jesus
will be lost against Jesus' wish

choices.why: ἐκλαμβάνω means to take or interpret; 'badly' keeps the adverbial force of κακῶς and the participial clause's causal sense.

pass_b_english: We must understand that the earlier friends of the gospel's letter, who did not notice that Jesus spoke these things in parables and that they were said by the Spirit, leveled out the third kind to match the first two. For if the two are spoken bodily, it follows that the third is bodily as well. The second group applied to the third kind a sound interpretation, thinking that the cutting out of the passionate part from the soul by reason is what is meant, but they no longer saw that it was fitting to take the first two allegorically as well. And if it is possible to say in other places, "The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life" (2 Corinthians 3:6), the same must be said here: the kept line about the two eunuchisms killed those who understood the third in the same way. If anyone wants to show from other examples that the New Testament has a letter that kills, let him hear how the Savior says to the apostles: "When I sent you out without a purse, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?" (Luke 22:35) Then he says, "Now let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a bag, and let the one who has none sell his cloak and buy a sword" (Luke 22:36). For the one who does not understand and buys a murderous sword will perish against the will of Jesus, having taken the word badly. Glory to Christ. Amen.

problems.source_quote: Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων, μή τινος ὑστερήσατε;
problems.why: The verse reference is incorrect: this is Luke 10:4, not Luke 22:35. Luke 22:35-36 has similar wording but is a different context (Last Supper discourse, not the mission charge). The source quotes the mission charge.
problems.ruling: Source quotes Luke 10:4 mission charge (ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας); Luke 22:35 is Last Supper, different context.

fixed: Changed verse reference from Luke 22:35 to Luke 10:4; the source quote matches the mission charge in Luke 10:4, not the Last Supper discourse in Luke 22:35.

problems.source_quote: Ὅτε ἀπέστειλα ὑμᾶς ἄτερ βαλλαντίου καὶ πήρας καὶ ὑποδημάτων, μή τινος ὑστερήσατε;
problems.why: The quotation matches Luke 22:35, not Luke 10:4; Luke 10:4 says 'carry no purse, no bag, no sandals' as a command, but this asks 'did you lack anything?'

fixed: The quotation 'When I sent you out without a purse, bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?' matches Luke 22:35, not Luke 10:4; corrected the citation.

last_rejected.why: ἐξωμάλισαν means 'made level/smooth' in sense of 'forced into conformity,' not 'leveled out' as flattened/destroyed; but worse, the English obscures that they made the third conform to the first two by treating all three bodily.
last_rejected.fix: they smoothed the third kind into conformity with the first two
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξωμάλισαν means 'leveled/made conform'; 'leveled out...to match' correctly conveys conformity. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ τηρηθεῖσα περὶ τῶν δύο εὐνουχισμῶν γραμμὴ
last_rejected.why: τηρηθεῖσα γραμμὴ means 'the literal reading/observance' or 'the line preserved in its literal sense,' not 'kept line'; it refers to maintaining the literal interpretation of the first two.
last_rejected.fix: the literal observance regarding the two eunuchisms
last_rejected.ruling: τηρηθεῖσα γραμμὴ = 'kept line/preserved line'; 'kept line' is within normal range, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: killed those who understood the third in the same way
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀπέκτεινε τοὺς τὸν τρίτον ὡσαύτως νοήσαντας
last_rejected.why: The Greek says the literal reading killed those who understood the third 'in the same way' (i.e., literally, like the first two), but English 'in the same way' is ambiguous; it could mean the same people were killed, not the same manner of understanding.
last_rejected.fix: killed those who took the third in the same literal sense
last_rejected.ruling: ὡσαύτως νοήσαντας = 'understood in the same way'; English 'in the same way' correctly modifies understanding. Not ambiguous.

last_rejected.why: τὸν λόγον here refers to the specific saying/statement about the sword, not 'the word' in a general sense; and ἐκλαβών means 'understanding/interpreting,' not 'taking.'
last_rejected.ruling: τὸν λόγον = 'the word/saying'; ἐκλαβών = 'taking/understanding'; both within normal range. No meaning changed.
